prompts.slash: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent pixel-art RPG greatsword jump-cleave effect source atlas, FOUR columns by TWO rows, eight separate complete square frames, generous transparent gutters. Match the supplied reference's sharp pure white/silver thick ribbons, charcoal outline and chipped tapered fins. The current native gameplay screenshots demonstrate the WRONG effect: a rotated sideways white slash to the side of the vertical sword. Create ORIGINAL direction-specific perspective art aligned along the actual vertical blade instead. Row 1: UP / AWAY from the camera, release along screen-up direction: a broad hooked white wedge reaches toward a far-floor endpoint near upper center, the curved blade trail extends back toward lower-left near foreground. Row 2: DOWN / TOWARD camera, release along screen-down: a wide forceful hooked white wedge reaches near-floor endpoint near lower center, trail extends from upper-right background. These are separately drawn views with fore-shortening and curved volume, not straight beams or rotated copies of side slashes. Four-frame progression for each: narrow bright release, maximal broad thick white curved cleave, strong taper with chips, small fading shards. Impact endpoint is fixed for all four frames within each row. Put ONE tiny magenta registration cross at the impact endpoint in each source cell: UP row at 50% cell width and 22% cell height; DOWN row at 50% width and 78% height. The guide is removed during offline import, not part of the effect. All artwork fits inside its own cell with wide gutters and no adjacent fragments. Include no people, sword, scenery, UI, labels, letters, borders, glowing circles, gold, red or cyan. True transparent background. Crisp chunky pixel contours and restrained three-tone shading; match reference motif, keep animation visual radius consistent.
prompts.ground: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent pixel-art RPG sword impact FLOOR burst atlas, FOUR columns by TWO rows, eight complete square source cells with generous transparent gutters. Use supplied reference white/silver chipped slash motif and charcoal outlines. Draw original UP and DOWN directional ground effects viewed from top-down three-quarter RPG camera: small low WHITE/SILVER dust fans, angular stone chips and short branching floor fissures around a visibly foreshortened oval footprint. No straight horizontal UI line or side-on wall of spikes. Row 1 UP/away: fan and fissures travel away screen-up, narrower distant end, dust lies low on the floor; row 2 DOWN/toward: fan opens toward lower foreground, broader near end. Four frames each: compact contact spark with first fissures; low powerful spread; scattered chips/dust widening; sparse fading residual chips. The actual sword contact point remains identical across all frames in each row. Add one tiny magenta registration cross at that point centered horizontally, at 60% of cell height in every cell, removed during import. Keep the whole oval footprint and all chips fully inside the source cell. Match reference silver-white plus cool charcoal grey, crisp pixel edges, no cyan, no gold, no rings or runes, no characters, no blade, no scenery, no text, no grid lines or borders. True transparency. Directional floor depth is essential; do not rotate an existing side burst into a vertical panel.
